d4d_fields.description: CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset generated by the Bridge2AI CHoRUS data generation project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium, under NIH award OT2OD032701. Data are collected retrospectively from intensive care admissions at contributing hospitals and are held under controlled access in a cloud enclave. The project website reports a currently released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, comprising 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized electronic health record data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data; a September 2025 training webinar instead reported over 45,000 unique admissions across 14 hospitals as of August 2025. The anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals, assembled by a consortium of more than 60 members across 20 institutions. Nine data modalities are documented - demographics, medication administration (time-stamped at each infusion change or dose administration), procedures, nursing flowsheets (high-frequency documentation), diagnoses, clinical notes (extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit), imaging from PACS, waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware, and waveform EEG from hospital databases. Structured EHR data and telemetry sit in the shared enclave; clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites with only tokens shared. The project also states an intention to sequester a holdout test set for external validation of models.

instances.instance_type: Patient admission from an intensive care unit (ICU), pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
instances.notes: Figure for the current released dataset. The anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions.
instances.source_caveats: Sources disagree on admission volume. The project website (tier 2, documentation) reports 50,000 admissions in the current released dataset; the cohort 2 informational webinar (tier 4) states that as of August 2025 the dataset covered 14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions. The higher-ranked project website value is stated here.

instances.instance_type: Clinical note, extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit
instances.notes: Notes are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens are placed in the shared enclave. Published metadata follows the OHNLP open-source schema; as of August 2025 the metadata entry for this modality was marked planned.

instances.instance_type: Admission with radiology imaging data obtained from hospital PACS
instances.notes: The project website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current released dataset. Imaging follows the DICOM schema; metadata was marked planned as of August 2025.
instances.source_caveats: The two sources count different units and were both retained rather than reconciled: the project website (tier 2) reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data, while the cohort 2 webinar (tier 4) states that as of August 2025 imaging was "currently 1000 images available with de-id in process for larger cohort".

instances.instance_type: Waveform telemetry recording from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware
instances.notes: Stored in WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema. The project website reports 23 Tb of waveform data in the current released dataset.

instances.instance_type: Waveform EEG recording from hospital EEG databases
instances.notes: Stored as EDF+ and Persyst; extraction was in process as of August 2025 and the metadata entry was marked planned.

d4d_fields.source_caveats: Four sources were used, ranked: the CHoRUS project website (project_documentation, tier 2), the NIH RePORTER project page for OT2OD032701 (tier 4), the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Cohort 2 informational webinar of September 2025 (tier 4), and a 2025-11-14 capture of the chorus-ai GitHub organization overview (tier 5). The 2022 award abstract is written in the future tense about project plans and is recorded here as intention rather than as current dataset state. Volume figures differ between the tier-2 website (50,000 released admissions) and the tier-4 webinar (over 45K unique admissions as of August 2025); the higher-ranked figure is stated with the disagreement noted at the affected instance. The webinar's imaging figure (1,000 images) and the website's (7,642 admissions with radiology data) count different units and are both retained. The 23 Tb waveform figure is reported for waveform data only, so no dataset-wide size is recorded. The cohort 2 webinar lists six people under the heading "Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team" with institutions but no individual role descriptions; only Eric Rosenthal is independently attested as principal investigator, by the NIH RePORTER project page, and principal_investigator is the only person-valued field the Creator class declares, so it carries each listed leader. The bundle states that CHoRUS is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and collaborates with the other three, but names no sibling dataset, so no dataset relationships are recorded.
